title: How to Calculate How Many Khaprail Tiles Your Roof Needs
excerpt: How to work out how many khaprail tiles your roof needs: measure the sloped area, find one tile's exposed coverage, divide and add an allowance.
focus_keyword: how many khaprail tiles per square foot
meta_title: How Many Khaprail Tiles Per Square Foot? Calculator
meta_description: How many khaprail tiles per square foot? Learn the simple method: roof area, exposed coverage of one tile and an allowance. Get a free Pak Clay sample.
answer_box: The number of khaprail tiles per square foot depends on the profile, because each tile hides part of itself under the next row. Divide your sloped roof area by the exposed coverage of one sample tile, then add roughly 5 to 10 percent for cuts and breakage.
ai_summary: There is no single khaprail tile count per square foot, because overlap changes how much roof each tile covers. Measure the sloped roof area, find the exposed coverage of a real sample, divide, and add an allowance. Pak Clay, making clay products in Lahore since 1982, offers free samples for measuring.
author: Pak Clay Team

faqs.question: How much does it cost to tile a roof with khaprail?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on tile count, unit price, structure, labour, transport and breakage. Build your own all-in figure from dated written quotes rather than a tile-only rate.

faqs.question: Is it better to count tiles per piece or per square foot?
faqs.answer: Either works if the unit is clear. Per-square-foot quotes depend on the exposed coverage used, so ask which overlap and area the seller assumed before comparing.

faqs.question: How much extra should I order?
faqs.answer: About 5 to 10 percent is commonly used, and roofs with many hips, valleys or cut edges may need more. Ask your contractor and write the allowance into the quote.

faqs.question: Should I measure the floor plan or the roof surface?
faqs.answer: Measure the sloped roof surface. A sloped roof has more area than its footprint, and a steeper roof has a larger gap. Ask a contractor to calculate it from the pitch if unsure.
